**Explanation (3-5 sentences):**
The pawn check on f5 is devastating because it forces White's king to respond to check, but crucially leaves the rook on a7 undefended. Whether White captures the pawn with Kxf5 or retreats to Ke5, Black simply plays Rxa7, winning the rook. The key lesson: when your opponent has a piece far from the action (like that rook), look for forcing moves—checks or captures—that exploit the undefended piece's position. Always calculate checks first!
